mechanism: The level-1 codeword choice of the baseline RQ-VAE is re-scored by a fixed derived Poincare distance minus a frozen train-only behaviour offset: the offset turns each level-1 codeword into a popularity-adjusted directed-transition surplus (a PMI-style m_i aggregated by the soft level-1 assignment), normalised to its own mean, and weighted by a geodesic scale measured once in epoch 1. The curvature is not swept: c = (rho/s)^2 with rho = 0.5 the proposal's fixed dimensionless radius-to-scale ratio and s the training-split RMS of the per-item latent NORM measured at step 0. The CODE of levels 2 and 3, of the residual recursion, of the reconstruction codebook and of the straight-through estimator is byte-identical to the baseline (their INPUTS differ, because the level-1 choice differs); reconstruction uses the UNLIFTED codeword a_{k1}. The behaviour channel and the curvature act on one expression, score_k = DIST(LIFT(r), LIFT(a_k)) - off_k.

computations.name: scale
inputs: the baseline encoder's latents z_i (train items, D-dim) at step 0
computations.output: s (a scalar) and the curvature c = (rho/s)^2
computations.definition: s = sqrt( mean over the training items i of ||z_i||_2^2 ), the RMS of the per-item latent VECTOR NORM (not a per-coordinate RMS, which would be ||z||_2/sqrt(D) and would multiply the tanh argument by sqrt(D)). It is measured once at step 0 and frozen. rho = 0.5 is the fixed ratio of the latent scale to the ball radius: rho = s/R_c, so R_c = s/rho = 2s; the curvature is c = (rho/s)^2 = 0.25/s^2 (units 1/||.||^2). c is never an input and never tuned. FAIL-CLOSED: if s is not finite or s <= 0 the run stops with an error; s is never replaced by a default, because a silent default would change the curvature the mechanism claims.
computations.note: measured on the training split at step 0 only; frozen

computations.name: lift
inputs: a residual r (B, D) or a codebook vector a (K1, D)
computations.output: the lifted point u = LIFT(r) or q = LIFT(a)
computations.definition: LIFT(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)*||v||) * v / (sqrt(c)*||v|| + eps) with eps = 1e-12, and LIFT(0) = 0 because the numerator v vanishes (the eps guard only keeps the division finite; there is NO separate zero-norm branch). At c = 0 LIFT is the identity map (the GEOMETRY_OFF arm). The lift is applied to the residual and to the codebook vector SEPARATELY, never to their difference.

computations.name: distance
computations.domain: c > 0 for the curved arm; both arguments lifted, so c||x||^2 < 1 and c||y||^2 < 1
computations.definition: MOBIUS(x,y) = ((1 + 2c<x,y> + c||y||^2)x + (1 - c||x||^2)y) / (1 + 2c<x,y> + c^2||x||^2||y||^2 + eps); DIST(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh( min( sqrt(c)*||MOBIUS(-x,y)||, 1 - 1e-6 ) ), the idea's exact expression, with the clamp as the ONLY numerical guard on the artanh argument (the lift approaches the ball boundary as tanh -> 1, so a float latent can round onto it). eps = 1e-12 appears in the Mobius denominator only; the norm carries no eps. At c = 0, DIST(x,y) = 2||x - y||.
computations.note: the idea's expression, with the eps in the Mobius denominator and the min(., 1 - 1e-6) clamp on the artanh argument, exactly as the SymPy surface states

computations.name: level-1 score
computations.definition: D_k = DIST(u, q_k); score_k = D_k - off_k. The curvature supplies D_k, the behaviour side supplies off_k, and score_k cannot be formed without both.
computations.note: the single coupling surface: the executable statements carry it end to end (lift, distance, demand, weight, offset, score, assignment, residual)

computations.name: level-1 assignment
computations.definition: k1 = argmin_k score_k, ties resolved to the smallest k. The assignment is discrete; the encoder gradient reaches the model through the baseline's straight-through estimator on the chosen code, exactly as in the baseline.

computations.name: residual recursion
inputs: the chosen UNLIFTED codebook vector a_{k1}
computations.output: r_next (B, D), the input of level 2
computations.definition: r_next = r - a_{k1}: the unmodified baseline codeword vector, not LIFT(a_{k1}) and not the offset-adjusted position. The recursion's CODE is the baseline's; its input r_next differs from the baseline's only because the level-1 choice differs. LIFT(a_{k1}) enters only inside score_k.

computations.name: behaviour demand
inputs: the training-split consecutive-pair count matrix t_ij (N, N)
the current level-1 soft assignment p_ik (N, K1) of the training items
computations.definition: From TRAINING-SPLIT sessions only: directed counts t_ij for consecutive pairs (i consumed before j, self-pairs dropped); out_i = sum_j t_ij and in_j = sum_i t_ij are that graph's degrees; eps = 1e-12. m_i = sum_j [ t_ij / sqrt(out_i * in_j + eps) ] over j = 1..N (the summation is INSIDE, so the value is well defined). Per epoch, with the CURRENT level-1 codes of the training items, a minibatch of B items gives p_ik = softmax_k(-D_ik / tau) with tau = 1, shape (B, K1). The epoch aggregate sums over ALL N training items: num_k = sum over the batches of (p_ik * m_i[:, None]).sum(0) and den_k = sum over the batches of p_ik.sum(0), then b_raw_epoch_k = num_k / (den_k + eps), shape (K1,) - an item-weighted mean, never a mean of per-batch means. Then, ONCE PER EPOCH at the end of the epoch, b_raw <- (1 - eta) * b_raw + eta * b_raw_epoch, eta = 0.1, initialised to 1 for every codeword, detached and no_grad; b_k = log(1 + b_raw_k / mean_k(b_raw_k)). The soft assignment p_ik uses D_ik, the PURE geodesic distance, not score_k: that is the idea's definition of the behaviour channel. Because b_raw holds its initial value 1 until the first end-of-epoch update, EVERY epoch-1 batch has b_raw = 1 for all k, hence b_k = log 2 for all k and a k-independent offset; the offsets separate only from epoch 2. The EMA applies to b_raw, never to b_k.
computations.note: training split only; no validation, test or future behaviour

computations.name: offset weight
inputs: min_k D_k of every training item of epoch 1 (the source of mean_scale)
num_k and den_k accumulated over the training items of epoch 1
computations.output: w, recomputed at the END of every epoch from the frozen mean_scale and that epoch's b_k, then held constant during the next epoch
computations.definition: The specification COMPLETES the idea here: the idea fixes mean_scale as the epoch-1 running mean of min_k D_k and says nothing about w during epoch 1, when that mean does not exist yet. The completion is w = 0 during epoch 1 (hence off_k = 0 and a pure geodesic assignment), which is immaterial to the score because the epoch-1 offsets are k-independent anyway. mean_scale = the ITEM-WEIGHTED mean of min_k D_k over the training items of epoch 1 (not a mean of per-batch means), in the CURRENT branch's distance (the Euclidean 2||u-q|| when GEOMETRY_OFF, so the switch stays scale-consistent), FROZEN from epoch 2 on. From epoch 2 on, w = rho_off * mean_scale / max_k log(1 + b_k) with rho_off = 0.10 (documented default), recomputed at the END of every epoch from the frozen mean_scale and that epoch's b_k and held constant during the next epoch, in step with the b_raw update.
computations.note: no constant is swept: mean_scale is measured once, rho_off is the proposal's documented default

computations.name: offset
computations.definition: off_k = w * log(1 + b_k) with b_k from 'behaviour demand' (NOT b_raw_k: using b_raw would change both the offset scale and w's normaliser). During epoch 1 this is 0 because w = 0. With BEHAVIOUR_OFF the implementation sets off_k = 0 for every k on the FLAG itself, never on a computed maximum.
computations.note: the b consumed by score_k, off_k and max_k log(1+b_k) is b_k

computations.name: objective
inputs: the baseline reconstruction and commitment terms
computations.output: the scalar loss the baseline optimiser minimises
computations.definition: loss = baseline_recon + baseline_commit, byte-identical to the baseline, with the straight-through estimator on the chosen code. The mechanism adds NO new loss term: it changes which codeword is chosen, so the baseline objective trains a different quantisation and the encoder gradient flows through the baseline's reconstruct-path STE on a_{k1} exactly once.
computations.note: no auxiliary loss, no extra optimiser

inputs: r, the residual entering level 1 (B, D) - the baseline's r
the level-1 codebook a (K1, D) - the baseline's, learned, never detached
the training-split counts t_ij (N, N) and the per-item mass m_i (N,), train only
the demand b_raw (K1,) carried across epochs, detached, no_grad
the frozen scale s, curvature c and mean_scale
outputs: k1, the level-1 codeword index for every residual (B,)
the demand b_k (K1,) and the offset off_k (K1,) as diagnostics
parameters: rho = 0.5, the fixed ratio of the latent scale to the ball radius (R_c = s/rho = 2s)
s = the training-split RMS of the per-item latent norm at step 0; c = (rho/s)^2
rho_off = 0.10, the proposal's documented offset strength
eta = 0.1, the demand EMA momentum; tau = 1, the soft assignment temperature
the demand buffer b_raw (K1,): detached, no_grad, initialised to one and updated once per epoch (NOT frozen)
the frozen mean_scale: the item-weighted mean of min_k D_k over epoch 1, constant from epoch 2

dimensions.t_ij: N x N over all N training items
dimensions.m_i: N, the per training item mass
dimensions.p_ik: B x K1 for one minibatch; num_k and den_k aggregate it over the N epoch items

gradient_rules.operator: the mechanism's constants (rho, s, c, rho_off, eta, tau)
gradient_rules.rule: no gradient: they are constants, and b_raw and mean_scale are detached buffers, so no mechanism quantity is learned
the argmin has no gradient; the reconstruction gradient reaches the encoder through the baseline's straight-through estimator on the chosen code a_{k1}
trained exactly as the baseline trains it; the distance and the offset never appear in a differentiable loss, they only select k1

encoder_gradient: perturbing a training item's feature must change the encoder's gradient through the reconstruction path's straight-through estimator on a_{k1}, and must not change it when only that STE link is removed; the baseline commitment term keeps its own gradient and is not part of this test

training_integration.loss: baseline_recon + baseline_commit, unchanged, straight-through on a_{k1}
training_integration.reconstruction: the chosen codeword at its baseline position: reconstruction and the residual use a_{k1} UNLIFTED, consistent with r_next = r - a_{k1}; LIFT(a_{k1}) enters only inside score_k
training_integration.optimizer: the baseline's, unchanged; no new parameter group

switches: BEHAVIOUR_OFF (present in code, never trained): m_i = 1 for every item, so b_raw_k = sum_i p_ik / (sum_i p_ik + eps) = 1 to within eps for every k (not exactly 1), b_k = log 2 to within eps for every k, and the offset would be a k-INDEPENDENT constant to within eps - a constant shift cannot change argmin_k score_k. The implementation therefore sets off_k = 0 exactly, on the FLAG, so the assignment is pure geodesic nearest neighbour in the derived ball.

GEOMETRY_OFF (present in code, never trained): c = 0, so LIFT is the identity and DIST(x,y) = 2||x - y||; the score is 2||r - a_k|| - w*log(1 + b_k). The demand stays ENABLED but is recomputed from the Euclidean distances (p_ik = softmax_k(-2||u-q_k||/tau), hence b_raw and b_k change), and mean_scale is the EUCLIDEAN item-weighted mean of min_k 2||u-q_k|| over epoch 1, so w stays scale-consistent.

BOTH_ON: the single formal run - c = (rho/s)^2 with the lift and the geodesic distance, plus the frozen train-only offset with its derived weight. Trained once: no sweep, no seed repetition, no early stopping.
excluded: any use of validation, test or future behaviour in the demand
any learned profile, attention, or per-codeword curvature parameter
any denoising or autoencoding pretraining; the RQ-VAE trains as baseline
any extra loss term, auxiliary head or second geometry
any sweep, ablation training run or seed repetition

executable_statements: def lift(v, c): return v if c == 0.0 else v * (torch.tanh(math.sqrt(c) * _norm(v)) / (math.sqrt(c) * _norm(v) + eps)).unsqueeze(-1)

def mobius(x, y, c): return ((1 + 2 * c * (x * y).sum(-1, keepdim=True) + c * (y * y).sum(-1, keepdim=True)) * x + (1 - c * (x * x).sum(-1, keepdim=True)) * y) / (1 + 2 * c * (x * y).sum(-1, keepdim=True) + c * c * (x * x).sum(-1, keepdim=True) * (y * y).sum(-1, keepdim=True) + eps)
def dist(x, y, c): return 2.0 * _norm(x - y) if c == 0.0 else (2.0 / math.sqrt(c)) * torch.atanh(torch.clamp(math.sqrt(c) * _norm(mobius(-x, y, c)), max=1.0 - 1e-6))
num_k = torch.zeros(K1); den_k = torch.zeros(K1)   # the epoch's accumulators
num_k = num_k + (p_ik * m_i[:, None]).sum(0)        # one batch
b_raw_epoch_k = num_k / (den_k + eps)              # once, at the epoch's end
b_raw = (1 - eta) * b_raw + eta * b_raw_epoch_k    # the carried buffer
mean_scale = ms_sum / ms_count                     # frozen from epoch 2
w = 0.0 if (BEHAVIOUR_OFF or epoch == 1) else rho_off * mean_scale / torch.log1p(b_k).max()
off_k = 0.0 if BEHAVIOUR_OFF else w * torch.log1p(b_k)
continuous_surface.note: The statements are the DISTANCE in SymPy: they are the equations the reference contract must equal, statement by statement. The executable_statements are the same surface as a program: the lift, the distance, the demand's accumulation, the weight and the score, in the order the trainer runs them. The carried buffers (b_raw, ms_sum, ms_count) live across the epoch and are stated here with the values they carry.

conventions.curvature: the ball is of curvature kappa = -c with c > 0; the ball radius is R_c = 1/sqrt(c) - a radius R with kappa = -1/R^2 is the same family under c = 1/R^2, and every distance, exponential map and radius must use ONE of them
conventions.distance: d_c(x, y) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c) ||(-x) (+) y||), with (+) the canonical Mobius sum; at c = 0 the limit is 2||x - y||, and the factor 2 is the metric's normalisation
conventions.exponential_map: exp_0^c(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)||v||) v / (sqrt(c)||v||), and exp_x^c(v) = x (+) [tanh(sqrt(c) lambda_x^c ||v|| / 2) v / (sqrt(c)||v||)] with lambda_x^c = 2/(1 - c||x||^2)
conventions.tangent_norm: a tangent vector's Euclidean coordinate norm is not its Riemannian norm: ||v||_{0,c} = lambda_0^c ||v|| = 2||v||, so d_c(0, exp_0^c(v)) = 2||v|| and log_0^c(exp_0^c(v)) = v
conventions.fréchet_mean: the Frechet mean of a weighted set is the point minimising the weighted sum of squared distances; a coordinate average may not be called a Frechet mean
conventions.straight_through: the assignment is an argmin and has no gradient; the reconstruction gradient reaches the encoder through the straight-through estimator x_q = x + (x_q - x).detach()
